summary: Review-required audit trail for the DISM-based component-store cleanup card. The live app already surfaces cleanup.component-store as a first-party command tweak, and repo docs point to the exact DISM cleanup flow, but this card has not yet been promoted into the validated research-provider surface.

setting.name: Cleanup Component Store
setting.casual_explanation: This runs the Windows component-store cleanup command to remove superseded servicing payloads and reclaim disk space.
setting.why_people_change_it: People run it when they want to reclaim disk space from the WinSxS component store after servicing and updates have accumulated.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The action is meant to reclaim disk space, but it is still a maintenance command rather than a normal on/off preference. This record currently documents the live app behavior and repo-backed provenance, but it is still held short of the validated research surface.
setting.professional_notes: The current app exposes a command-backed cleanup card that detects with DISM /AnalyzeComponentStore and applies DISM /StartComponentCleanup. Repo cleanup docs and tweak provenance both map this card to the same DISM maintenance action. The record stays review-required until this command-backed cleanup surface is promoted through the normal research validation path.

evidence.title: Current DISM cleanup implementation
evidence.summary: The engine tweak detects with DISM /AnalyzeComponentStore, applies with /StartComponentCleanup, verifies by checking whether cleanup is still recommended, and does not support rollback.

decision.why: The live app behavior and repo-backed DISM mapping are clear, but this command-backed cleanup card has not yet completed the research-surface validation path.
blocking_issues: The card still lives only in the first-party cleanup provider and has not been promoted into the research-provider surface.
This is an on-demand maintenance action with no rollback support.
decision.promotion_disposition_reason: Closed as rejected for research-provider promotion because the live action is one-shot, destructive, high-risk, reboot-sensitive, or lacks a rollback story suitable for a validated tweak card.
decision.promotion_reopen_criteria: Reopen only if the app gains a verified rollback/snapshot contract and dedicated validation proof for the exact action.

open_questions: Do we want a validated cleanup-command promotion lane that can surface one-shot DISM maintenance actions through the research provider?
Should this card stay operator-only even after it has a checked-in research record?
